assumptions: Click volume stays broadly similar during the test.
The enquiry form event definition stays unchanged for the whole test.
experiments.hypothesis: If the enquiry form event is verified as firing correctly and a simplified landing page variant is tested, the platform-attributed conversion rate may recover toward its earlier level of 2.1%.
experiments.measurement_method: Compare the platform-attributed conversion rate of each variant on the same Meta conversion basis, allowing for late-reported conversions before reading the result.
experiments.problem_statement: For [SYNTHETIC] Meta | CT | Prospecting, platform-attributed conversion rate fell from 2.1% to 0.94%, and there was a run with no attributed conversions from 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-26.
experiments.proposed_experiment: First check that the enquiry form submission event fires end to end. Then split traffic between the current landing page and a simplified form variant.
risks: If a tracking fault is found, data from before the fix may not be comparable with data after it.
Meta may restate recent days as late conversions are reported, which could shift the result.
experiments.title: Audit enquiry form tracking and test a landing page variant for Meta CT Prospecting

assumptions: The data-driven attribution settings stay unchanged during the test.
experiments.hypothesis: Moving budget away from high-cost, low-converting search terms may bring cost per platform-attributed conversion back toward GBP 52.77.
experiments.measurement_method: Compare cost per platform-attributed conversion between the experiment and control arms on the same Google Ads booking-request basis.
experiments.problem_statement: For [SYNTHETIC] Search | MRI | London, cost per platform-attributed conversion rose from GBP 52.77 to GBP 108.88, and ROAS fell from 6.83 to 3.31.
experiments.proposed_experiment: Run a campaign experiment that tightens match types and adds negative keywords for low-performing queries, compared against the unchanged campaign.
risks: Narrower targeting could reduce booking-request volume.
Changes in auction competition during the test could confound the comparison.
experiments.title: Test keyword and bid restructuring on Search MRI London

assumptions: Budget levels stay comparable across the test and control arms.
experiments.hypothesis: Refreshed asset groups and a clearer booking-request landing page may raise the platform-attributed conversion rate toward 2.9%.
experiments.measurement_method: Compare platform-attributed conversion rate between the test and control arms on the same Google Ads booking-request basis.
experiments.problem_statement: For [SYNTHETIC] PMax | CT | National, platform-attributed conversion rate fell from 2.9% to 1.3% while clicks went from 1671 to 1749.
experiments.proposed_experiment: Test a refreshed asset group with a dedicated booking-request landing page against the current setup, using a platform experiment split.
risks: The PMax learning phase may depress early results.
Placement mix may shift in ways the analyst cannot see.
experiments.title: Test asset group and landing page changes on PMax CT National

hypotheses.statement: Clicks on [SYNTHETIC] Meta | CT | Prospecting stayed close to their earlier level (1754 vs 1706), yet attributed conversions stopped from 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-26. This may point to a tracking or form issue with the 'Scan enquiry form submitted' event rather than to a change in audience interest.

[SYNTHETIC] Search | MRI | London received fewer clicks (1177 to 778) on similar spend. Higher click costs, for example from auction competition, could account for part of the rise in cost per conversion.
[SYNTHETIC] PMax | CT | National kept a similar click volume while its conversion rate fell. This may reflect lower-quality placements or a change in the landing or booking-request experience.
The strong attributed efficiency of [SYNTHETIC] Search | MRI | Brand could partly reflect existing brand demand that might convert without ads, so it may not indicate incremental impact.

limitations: Several findings concern the same campaigns and share inputs, so they should not be read as independent signals.
Some findings were suppressed by the noise guard and are not reflected here.
The Meta and Google conversion events measure different funnel stages and should not be compared directly.

observed_facts.statement: [SYNTHETIC] Meta | CT | Prospecting recorded a run of 6 consecutive days with spend and no platform-attributed conversions, from 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-26, with GBP 910.8 spent during that run.

For [SYNTHETIC] Meta | CT | Prospecting, comparing 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-30 with 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-10, cost per platform-attributed conversion rose from GBP 40.06 to GBP 93.62 (+134%). Conversion rate fell from 2.1% to 0.94%, while clicks went from 1754 to 1706.

For [SYNTHETIC] Search | MRI | London, cost per platform-attributed conversion rose from GBP 52.77 to GBP 108.88 (+106%) between the same windows. Clicks went from 1177 to 778 while spend went from GBP 4088.07 to GBP 4225.55.

For [SYNTHETIC] PMax | CT | National, platform-attributed conversion rate fell from 2.9% to 1.3% and platform-attributed ROAS fell from 8.09 to 3.69. Clicks went from 1671 to 1749 over the same windows.

[SYNTHETIC] Search | MRI | Brand had a cost per platform-attributed conversion of GBP 6.88 against a same-basis peer median of GBP 57.09. Its campaign ROAS was 55.19 against a peer median ROAS of 4.03.
For [SYNTHETIC] Search | Ultrasound | Manchester, platform-attributed ROAS fell from 5.18 to 3.19 (-39%), comparing 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-30 with 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-23.

publication.note: A previously generated, validated sample, published as static data. Request identifiers, budget reservations and ledger details were removed.
